steps.thought: Goal: the UI must show real collected data, with vendor/provisioned visible, then one real collection lands in the database. Question: what is the shortest path from the existing hook-based data layer to that, without adding a dependency?

Context7 (reactrouter, v6): loaders bind to a data router (createBrowserRouter). The app uses <BrowserRouter><Routes>, so adopting loaders is a router migration, not a data-layer tweak. Decision: keep useResource + dataSource, fix the missing fields instead. Recorded as a deliberate trade-off, not an oversight.

Gap analysis from grep: backend domain.Olt/Onu lack vendor_id, model, onu_type, interface_type, identity_source; the API never returns them, so the UI cannot show vendors no matter the data layer. Backend first, then types, then UI.

Implementation order: (a) add identity columns to domain.Onu + postgres scan, (b) mirror in TypeScript types, (c) UI: vendor column + Unprovisioned badge + vendor summary card, (d) prove by replaying captured rows into PGlite and curling the API — no device contact.

Replay of the captured rows into PGlite via ingest: 161 ONUs (133 provisioned, 28 status-only), 14 vendor ids. GET /dashboard/overview now returns vendorId/model/onuType/interfaceType/provisioned per ONU — so the UI's vendor column and Unprovisioned badge are fed by real shapes, not the fixture.

Closed: domain.Onu, the postgres scan and TypeScript types now carry vendorId/onuType/interfaceType/identitySource/thresholdModel/provisioned; the API returns them and the ONU pages render them. Confirmed by the replay + curl above, not inferred.
